script: Ismael Saibari just joined Bayern Munich from PSV for around 50 million euros, and one of the first things he did was pick his shirt number. He didn't go for something normal like seven or ten, he chose thirty-four. But that number was already carrying a weight almost nobody at Bayern understood. Ajax were playing a pre-season friendly against Werder Bremen back in July of 2017 when their twenty-year-old midfielder, Abdelhak Nouri, collapsed on the pitch. Everyone called him Appie, and he was the jewel of the Ajax academy, coming up alongside future stars like Frenkie de Jong and Matthijs de Ligt. Appie went into cardiac arrest, and because a defibrillator wasn't used on him quickly enough, he'd already suffered severe, permanent brain damage. He survived, but he hasn't been able to move on his own since that day, and the number he wore for Ajax was thirty-four. But Saibari isn't the only one who quietly refused to let Appie fade away. When Justin Kluivert signed for Roma, he took thirty-four and dedicated his first goal to Appie. And when Donny van de Beek joined Manchester United, he chose it too. Ajax then retired the number completely, an honor they'd only ever given to Johan Cruyff.
